newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares reach new record high in bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares reach new record high in bourse.

text.p: German shares surged to another record high on Friday as Wall Street's strongest bull run in history and a firm dollar propelled the market higher.

The 30-share DAX index was up 35.01 points to 3,743.00 points after earlier reaching a new record high at 3,751.26 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day trade, was up 4.55 points at 3,741.71 and reflected late Thursday's gains.

Other factors pushing the market higher were abating fears about the future of European monetary union as France and Germany appeared ready to reach a compromise on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the start of the new currency in January 1999.

"There is more and more confidence out there that the euro will come on time, even if it's weaker than expected, so people now expect that money will keep coming into Europe after currency union," a trader said.

"We are looking at some decent settlement scenarios at the moment. There could be short-term upsets -- the effect of wild rumours and possible political turmoil -- but we still should see money coming in," said the trader.
ABN Amro said in a report to clients that the outlook for the DAX index reaching 3,800 points looks "increasingly conservative" based on the market's recent heady surge.
"We'll take our cue now from Wall Street -- at least until this afternoon," one trader said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Index ended up 135.64 points, or 1.79 percent, at 7,711.47 points overnight.
Traders said German market gains came across the board and that no particular shares stood out early on.

SGL Carbon rose seven marks to 240.50 marks, recovering from losses since last Friday when U.S. and European Union regulators said SGL Carbon was part of a probe into possible price-fixing allegations for graphite electrodes.
